paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one. Famine is in the land, the stew has death in it, and the bread is twenty loaves for a hundred men (2 Kings 4:38, 40, 43). The stew and the bread are problems too big for the people standing around the pot. In both, the trouble lands in front of Elisha, the man of God, and the stew is made right and the bread goes around with some left over (2 Kings 4:41, 44).

Look at the two halves. In the first, a man gathers what he doesn't know, and the men cry out, "There is death in the pot, O man of God!" (2 Kings 4:40). They bring the trouble to Elisha, and nothing harmful is left in the pot (2 Kings 4:41). I think that's a good habit for a baker, friend: when something goes sideways, take it to God's man and don't just keep stirring, because I've burned plenty of batches by hiding them in the back of the oven and that never once helped.

In the second half, the math says no, but the LORD says, "They will eat and have some left over." (2 Kings 4:43). So they ate and had some left over, "according to the word of the LORD." (2 Kings 4:44). The lesson is that what God says, He does, even when the numbers look ridiculous. So the next time you're staring at a pot that's too small or a pile of loaves that's too short, remember that His word has the last say.
